sentences.text: This petition is filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from respondents on account of grievous injuries sustained by petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are; That, on 22-02-2019 at about 8.45 a.m., petitioner was riding his motorcycle, bearing No.KA-66-H-3248, on the left side of NH-206 Bypass road Bhadravathi,
near Vishwaraiah Cross, at that time, the driver of Omni Car, bearing No.KA-53-M-8551 came from his opposite direction extreme right side with high speed in rash and negligent manner endangering to human life, without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the motorcycle.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Maax Super Speciality Hospital,
Shivamoga, 3 (SCCH-16) MVC 29/2021 wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as Coconut Plucker and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and whereby lost his earning capacity.
Therefore, petitioner prayed for compensation.

3. In brief, the objections by respondent No.1 and 2 are that;
3(a).

In written statement of objections, respondent No.1 admitted the ownership of Maruthi Suzuki Omni Car, bearing No.KA-53-M-8551 and denied the petition averments generally and contended that the petitioner was riding the motorcycle without observing the traffic rules and regulations and accident had took place solely due to the carelessness and negligence of the petitioner himself, car,
bearing No.KA- 53-M-8551 was insured with respondent No.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident, the compensation claimed highly exorbitant, excessive and without any legal basis.
He prayed for dismissal of the petition.

3(b) Respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car, bearing No.KA-53-M- 8551 and denied the other petition averments generally and it contended that the accident had taken place due to actionable negligence on the part of petitioner himself.
Further, it sought for permission to contest 4 (SCCH-16) MVC 29/2021 even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. Based on the pleadings the following issues came to be framed:

Respondent No.2 did not lead its evidence except cross examining PWs and RW1.

sentences.text: The spot mahazar and sketch depict the scene of occurrence.
The MVA report shows the incident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.

The 7 (SCCH-16) MVC 29/2021 wound certificate reveals the petitioner sustained 1) deep cut lacerated wound over anterior part of neck 15x2 cm, 2) abrasion over right wrist joint, 3) abrasion over left foot, 4) mild abrasion over abdomen and 5) MRI cervical spine shows focal area of T2 hyperintensity at C5/C6 level S/O cord contusion,
mild subarachnoid space compression at C6/C5 level, normal bilateral brachial plexus, no E/o injury, 6) CT scan of brain plain shows acute SDH along with posterior falx and bilateral tentorium cerebilli, mild acute SAH in the prepontine and perimesencephalic cisterns, mild extracalvarial soft tissue swelling in the right frontal region.
The above said injury No.1 to 4 are simple and injury No.5 and 6 are grievous in nature.
The accident was not due to any mechanical defect in the sense, then that could have been by the negligence only.
Now whose negligence was there to the incident to be analyzed.
No independent eyewitness is examined herein.
The petitioner himself is as good as the eyewitness.
As already noted the final report shows the negligence was by the driver of the offended car.
The spot sketch corroborates the finality by the I.O.
Nothing is in elicitation by respondent No.2 in cross examination of petitioner in supportive of it's version regarding the negligence.
Under the scenario it is found there was no negligence by the petitioner to the incident.
Hence, without here being contrary evidence, here is no 8 (SCCH-16) MVC 29/2021 impediment to believe the police records.
Thus, police records are considered.

11. Regarding objection by respondent No.2 seeking permission u/sec 170 of MV Act is concerned, as respondent No.1 is contesting party the giving of permission under Section 170 of the MV Act, and discussion on the same now does not arise.

12. Wherefore, for the foregoing reasons, it establishes on preponderance of probability that the petitioner met with motor vehicle accident on 22.02.2018 at about 8.45 a.m., and sustained simple and grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Omni Car, bearing No.KA-53-M- 8551.
Hence, this issue answered in affirmative.

Wound certificate, which is at Ex.P4, reveals the injuries caused to the petitioner such as 1) deep cut lacerated wound over anterior part of neck 15x2 cm, 2) 9 (SCCH-16) MVC 29/2021 abrasion over right wrist joint, 3) abrasion over left foot,

6) CT scan of brain plain shows acute SDH along with posterior falx and bilateral tentorium cerebilli, mild acute SAH in the prepontine and perimesencephalic cisterns, mild extracalvarial soft tissue swelling in the right frontal region.
According to it the above said injury No.1 to 4 are simple and injury No.5 and 6 are grievous in nature.
Discharge summary, which is at Ex.P7 shows that the petitioner had taken conservative treatment as an inpatient for a period of 11 days in Maax Super Speciality Hospital.
It is averred that because of the injuries he suffered the disablement and from which he lost or lessen his earning capacity.

In proof of the disablement he examined PW2 - Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon and Spine Surgeon from Shreyas Clinic, who assessed the disability of petitioner, opined that the petitioner suffered neurological and neuropsychological disability at 63.91%.

His evidences clear that he is not the treated doctor and he had taken into consideration the informations given by the brother-in-law of petitioner in the assessment.
Under the facts and circumstances of case, considering the elicitation in cross examination of doctor, having regard to the nature of injuries, and the 10 (SCCH-16) MVC 29/2021 petitioner himself faced the cross examination and responded suitably the disability to the whole body is taken to be considered at 50% as disablement as the disability assessed is an opinion of the doctor and no certificate of disability is produced from the competent authority.
Avocation
It is averred that the petitioner was working as Coconut Plucker.
However, no document is forthcoming regarding avocation of petitioner is concerned.
Hence it is not established that the petitioner was working as Coconut Plucker, hence in the present case, avocation of petitioner is need to be considered notionally as he had notional income only.
Age As per Ex.P4 - wound certificate and discharge summary, age of petitioner was 25 years at the time of incident.
Hence, they are considered.
Income
As discussed on the head of avocation, the petitioner's avocation taken to be considered notionally.
In this regard as per the resolution of hon'ble the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, dated 17-02- 2022 notional income for the year 2019 came to be fixed at Rs.14,000/.
In the present case, under the facts and circumstances of the case, Rs.14,000/- is taken to 11 (SCCH-16) MVC 29/2021 be considered as notional income of the petitioner, per month.
Considering the avocation and income notionally now loss of future income due to disability needs to be calculated.
According to the determined age of petitioner multiplier is 18.

So, 50% of monthly notional income comes to Rs.7,000/- x 12 months x multiplier 18 = Rs.15,12,000/- it is considered Sri Manjunatha H vs Sri Chandrappa on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82926369/

sentences.text: Laid up period and Pain and sufferings
Petitioner was treated as inpatient from 22-02- 2019 to 04-03-2019.
He suffered pains and sufferings and also lost his earnings at the time of his treatment as well as his nourishment at least for the period of 6 months.
It is therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation considering his pains and sufferings and for his laid up period.

Hence, it is opined that 6 months' notional income of Rs.84,000/- + Rs.1,00,000/- for pains and sufferings =
Rs.1,84,000/- will be just and proper in compensation for laid up period and pain and sufferings.
Medical Bills:
It is averred that petitioner spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards the medical expenses.
To prove the same, he produced 35 medical bills and 28 prescriptions as per Ex.P8 and Ex.P9.
All those bills 12 (SCCH-16) MVC 29/2021 have been examined with care and caution and found correct.
There is no contra evidence to disbelieve the genuineness of these bills.
Hence, a sum of Rs.1,15,929/- is awarded towards medical expenses.

Amenities and happiness:
It is established that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
The assessment of disability by the doctor and its consideration as discussed above are considered herein.
With such permanent disablement and surgical scars he will have to lead his future life.
From such injury he suffered pains, difficulties, which deprived him of leading his happy life and from enjoying amenities.
It is therefore, the petitioner is entitle for compensation for loss of his such amenities and happiness.
So, It is deemed proper to award compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

Food, Nourishment, Attendant charges and Conveyance:
Under the facts and circumstances of the case having considered the nature of the injuries and permanent disablement, though here is no document particularly, it could be presumed that the petitioner might have spent considerable amount for his nutritional food, nourishment, attendant charges and conveyance.
It is therefore, it is opined that for such food, nourishment, attendant charges and for conveyance is concerned awarding of Rs.50,000/- as 13 (SCCH-16) MVC 29/2021 compensation is just and proper.
Hence, it is considered so.
Future medical expenses :
There is no evidence as far as future medical expenses is concerned.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.

14 (SCCH-16) MVC 29/2021 Liability:
16.
Insurance policy and its validity are admitted and no breaches are established by the insurer.
As found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of driver of the offended car.
On vicarious liability respondent No.1 being the owner is responsible, respondent No.2 being the insurer of respondent No.1 contractually liable to pay compensation.
Thus, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, initially respondent No.2 is liable to pay the determined compensation.
The petitioner is only entitled to such compensation and not fully as claimed for.
Accordingly, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
17.
In view of the findings, the petition deserves to be allowed in part.
Hence, the following order is passed:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to  compensation of Rs.19,62,000/-
(Rupees nineteen lakhs and sixty two thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 -Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
